Case Manager II - Canyon Vista

Telecare's mission is to deliver excellent and effective behavioral health services that engage individuals in recovering their health, hopes, and dreams. Telecare continues to advance cultural diversity, humility, equity, and inclusion at all levels of our organization by hiring mental health peers, BIPOC, LGBTQIA+, veterans, and all belief systems.

Canyon Vista is a 57 unit transitional and permanent supportive housing (PSH) program serving adults in San Mateo County with serious mental illness. Telecare will provide onsite case management, housing stabilization and rehabilitative services to tenants living in transitional and PSH units. Services onsite will be available 24 hours a day, 7 days per week.

Shift Available

PM, .6,  Part Time, Thursday- Saturday;   3:00 pm to 11:30 pm

Expected starting wage is $23.68. This position is covered by a collective bargaining agreement and is subject to union membership requirements upon hire.

Under direct supervision, serves as a primary support and case manager for individuals with mental illness and other co-occurring disorders by assisting them to live as independently as possible in their chosen community.

Required:

High School Graduation or G.E.D. equivalent and two (2) years of direct services in Mental Health OR community services; or Associates degree and one (1) year of experience OR Bachelor’s degree in Social Services
Sensitivity to multi-cultural populations and issues is required
Must be at least 18 years of age
Must be CPR, Crisis Prevention Institute (CPI), and First Aid certified on date of employment or within 60 days of employment and maintain current certification throughout employment

Additional regulatory, contractual or local requirements may apply

Preferred

Four (4) years’ experience in a mental health setting
Experience in providing intensive case management, intensive community supports using biopsychosocial rehabilitation concepts is highly desirable
Experience in a mental health setting, outpatient clinic, dual diagnosis treatment or community mental health service preferred

Essential Functions

Demonstrate the Telecare mission, purpose, values and beliefs in everyday language and contact with the internal and external stakeholders
Collaborate with members served to create Recovery Plan goals
Ensure all services described in the Recovery Plan are provided
Work effectively as part of a multidisciplinary team
Facilitate groups according to the needs and interests of members served
Provide appropriate interventions in crisis situations

Collect required data and complete required documentation
Coordinate transitions to lower levels of care
Maintain awareness of community resources and assist members served in appropriate use of community resources
Assist members served with all needs, including Activities of Daily Living
Assist members served in making and getting to essential appointments
Assist and advocate for members served in obtaining appropriate benefits; provide representative payee services
Ensure that members served understand their legal status and rights
Help members served achieve greater independence and autonomy
Safeguard confidentiality; adhere to HIPAA policies

Effective written and verbal communication skills
Organization/Time management skills
Good computer/technology skills
Ability to assess safety risks
Ability to gain trust and build rapport with diverse populations
Excellent driving skills
Knowledge of basic medical and psychiatric terminology

jobs.title: Pediatric ABA Program Manager
jobs.description:
Help Kids Show The World How Awesome They Are

Every kid we work with already has something remarkable in them. Some days it's a first word. Other days it's a calm transition, a high-five with a sibling, or a full meal at the family table without a meltdown. Our job is to clear the path so the world gets to see it.

At DV Therapy, we call our approach Fan First. We're not here to collect clients. We're here to earn fans: families who see their child making progress and feel like true partners in it, not just recipients of a service. That only happens when the programs behind the sessions are thoughtful, data-driven, and built for a real kid in a real home.

That's where you come in. As a Program Manager, you'll take your supervising BCBA's clinical direction and turn it into plans that work. You'll find the pattern in the data, adjust a strategy before it stalls, and coach the technicians and parents who carry it forward every day. When a family tells us their kid did something they weren't sure they'd ever see, your fingerprints will be on it.

Why Program Managers Choose DV Therapy

$30.00 – $33.00 per hour — your rate, with no bonus folded in to make the number look bigger
Leadership that came up through the work. Our COO, Mariah Prentice, started at DV Therapy as an SLPA nearly ten years ago and now runs operations for the whole company. Our founder and owner, Iddo deVries, MS, CCC-SLP, is a clinician too. Caseload and staffing decisions here get made by people who have carried a caseload.
A BCBA in your corner, not just on your org chart. You'll build programs side by side with your supervising BCBA, with clinical direction from our Clinical Director across all five sites. You get backup on the hard cases and a real voice in how plans are designed.
Want your BCBA? We'll help you get there. Supervised fieldwork hours toward certification, exam prep support, schedule flexibility for coursework: We're building our path to BCBA right now and we'd love for you to be one of the people who helps shape it.
Speech and OT down the hall. ABA, speech, and OT work as integrated pediatric teams in person, not referrals into a void. The feeding question, the AAC decision, the communication barrier behind a behavior — worked out in the hallway.
Clinic and in-home, so you see the whole picture. You'll split your time between our [Location] clinic and clients' homes. You see how a skill holds up at the kitchen table, not just at the therapy table.
Paid time off, paid holidays, and sick time
401(k) with a company match on up to 5%
Free, confidential mental health support through LifeCare, with 9 consultations a year. This job asks a lot of your heart, and we want you to have somewhere to put it down

What You'll Do

Design, evaluate, and refine individualized treatment plans with your supervising BCBA
Conduct functional behavior assessments and turn client data into clear next steps
Track progress and adjust interventions when the data says it's time
Train and supervise Behavior Technicians in the clinic and in the field
Coach parents and caregivers so progress carries over at home
Keep documentation accurate and reports on time
Join team meetings and keep growing through ongoing professional development

Master's degree in Applied Behavior Analysis or a related field
2+ years working with individuals with developmental disabilities or behavioral health needs
Hands-on experience developing ABA programs for children with autism and related diagnoses
Strength in parent training and social skills interventions
